title: He said that…: reported speech
intro: English shifts the tense when it reports: 'I'm tired' becomes 'she said she was tired'. Persian doesn't. It keeps the original tense and simply changes the person: گفت که خسته است – literally 'she said that she is tired'. In this lesson you learn to pass on messages, report questions with آیا and 'or not', report requests and orders with the subjunctive, and use a dozen verbs that say more than گفتن: explain, promise, insist, deny, warn.
goals: report what someone said without changing the tense: گفت که می‌آید
report yes/no questions with آیا or … یا نه, and wh-questions without changing the word order
report requests and orders with خواستن and the subjunctive: از ما خواست که صبر کنیم
use reporting verbs such as توضیح دادن، قول دادن، اصرار کردن، انکار کردن، هشدار دادن
recognise the perfect as the tense of hearsay: گفت که دیروز رفته است

sections.title: No tense shift
sections.md:
When English reports speech, it moves the verb back in time: *'I'm coming tomorrow'* → *he said he was coming*. Persian keeps the verb exactly as it was spoken and changes only the **person**:

- Mr Karimi: [[فردا می‌آیم.|fardā mi-āyam.|I'm coming tomorrow.]]
- Amir: [[گفت که فردا می‌آید.|goft ke fardā mi-āyad.|He said he would come tomorrow.]]

Literally, *he said that he comes tomorrow*. The word [[که|ke|that]] is optional, and in speech it is usually dropped: [[گفت فردا میاد|goft fardā miyād]].

This makes reported speech much easier than in English: no *was* for *is*, no *would* for *will*, no *had* for *has*. What you need instead is a good stock of **reporting verbs** – ask, answer, explain, promise, insist – and two small patterns for questions and requests.

items.en: landlord, landlady; owner of the house

items.note: present stem پرس; ask someone: از کسی پرسیدن

items.en: whether; marks a yes/no question in writing
to tell (a story), recount; to praise

sections.title: Same tense, new person
sections.md:
To report a statement, use [[گفتن|goftan]] (or another reporting verb) + optional [[که|ke]] + the sentence **in its original tense**. Change *I* to *he* or *she*, *you* to *I*, and so on – just as in English – but leave the tense alone.

One thing is different: when someone tells you about a **past** event, Persian very often reports it with the **perfect**: [[دیروز رفتم|diruz raftam|I went yesterday]] → [[گفت که دیروز رفته است|goft ke diruz rafte ast|he said he had gone yesterday]]. The perfect is the Persian tense of hearsay – of things you know only because someone told you. The simple past ([[گفت که دیروز رفت|goft ke diruz raft]]) is also correct.

In conversation people also quote directly, keeping the original *I*: [[گفت: «من فردا میام.»|goft: «man fardā miyām.»|he said, 'I'm coming tomorrow']]. The person ending of the verb tells you which one you are hearing.

sections.title: Reporting questions, requests and orders
sections.md:
**Yes/no questions.** In writing, put [[آیا|āyā|whether]] after [[پرسید که|porsid ke|he asked]]: [[پرسید که آیا می‌آیم|porsid ke āyā mi-āyam|he asked whether I was coming]]. In speech, leave out آیا and add [[یا نه|yā na|or not]] at the end: [[پرسید میام یا نه|porsid miyām yā na]].

**Wh-questions** keep their question word where it was – there is no change of word order, unlike English: [[کجا زندگی می‌کنی؟|kojā zendegi mi-koni?|where do you live?]] → [[پرسید کجا زندگی می‌کنم|porsid kojā zendegi mi-konam|he asked where I lived]]. Never use آیا here.

**Requests and orders** become a **subjunctive**: [[بنشین!|beneshin!|sit down!]] → [[گفت که بنشینم|goft ke beneshinam|he told me to sit down]]; [[لطفاً صبر کنید|lotfan sabr konid|please wait]] → [[از ما خواست که صبر کنیم|az mā khāst ke sabr konim|she asked us to wait]].

Mind the prepositions: you ask a question *from* someone ([[از کسی پرسیدن|az kas-i porsidan]]), ask *from* someone to do something ([[از کسی خواستن|az kas-i khāstan]]), but tell *to* someone ([[به کسی گفتن|be kas-i goftan]]).

sections.title: More precise than گفتن: reporting verbs
sections.md:
[[گفتن|goftan]] can report anything, but good Persian – and every news bulletin – uses more precise verbs. Almost all of them are compounds with [[کردن|kardan]] or [[دادن|dādan]], and all can be followed by [[که|ke]] and a clause.

Verbs that look forward to an action that has not happened yet – *promise, insist, suggest, ask (someone to do)* – take the **subjunctive**: [[قول داد که زود بیاید|ghowl dād ke zud biyāyad|he promised to come early]]. Verbs that report a fact – *explain, admit, deny, claim, announce* – keep the ordinary tense: [[اعتراف کرد که دروغ گفته است|e'terāf kard ke dorugh gofte ast|he admitted that he had lied]].

sections.title: The interview
sections.intro: Leila tells the story of her job interview – entirely in reported speech. Notice آیا in the yes/no questions, the subjunctive after خواستن and قول دادن, and the perfect for things that had already happened.

sentences.fa: لیلا دیروز برای کار در یک شرکت نرم‌افزاری مصاحبه داشت.
sentences.r: Leylā diruz barā-ye kār dar yek sherkat-e narm-afzāri mosāhebe dāsht.
sentences.en: Yesterday Leila had an interview for a job at a software company.
sentences.faV: لَیلا دیروز بَرایِ کار دَر یِک شِرکَتِ نَرم‌اَفزاری مُصاحِبه داشت.

sentences.fa: مدیر شرکت اول از او پرسید که چند سال سابقه‌ی کار دارد.
sentences.r: modir-e sherkat avval az u porsid ke chand sāl sābeghe-ye kār dārad.
sentences.en: The manager first asked her how many years of work experience she had.
sentences.faV: مُدیرِ شِرکَت اَوَّل اَز او پُرسید که چَند سال سابِقه‌یِ کار دارَد.

sentences.fa: لیلا گفت که پنج سال در یک بانک کار کرده است.
sentences.r: Leylā goft ke panj sāl dar yek bānk kār karde ast.
sentences.en: Leila said she had worked in a bank for five years.
sentences.faV: لَیلا گُفت که پَنج سال دَر یِک بانک کار کَرده اَست.

sentences.fa: مدیر پرسید چرا کار قبلی‌اش را رها کرده است.
sentences.r: modir porsid cherā kār-e ghabli-ash rā rahā karde ast.
sentences.en: The manager asked why she had left her previous job.
sentences.faV: مُدیر پُرسید چِرا کارِ قَبلی‌اَش را رَها کَرده اَست.

sentences.fa: لیلا توضیح داد که در آن بانک فرصتی برای پیشرفت نداشته است.
sentences.r: Leylā towzih dād ke dar ān bānk forsat-i barā-ye pishraft nadāshte ast.
sentences.en: Leila explained that at the bank she had had no chance to move up.
sentences.faV: لَیلا تَوضیح داد که دَر آن بانک فُرصَتی بَرایِ پیشرَفت نَداشته اَست.

sentences.fa: مدیر پرسید که آیا می‌تواند گاهی آخر هفته‌ها هم کار کند.
sentences.r: modir porsid ke āyā mi-tavānad gāhi ākhar-e hafte-hā ham kār konad.
sentences.en: The manager asked whether she could sometimes work at weekends too.
sentences.faV: مُدیر پُرسید که آیا می‌تَوانَد گاهی آخَرِ هَفته‌ها هَم کار کُنَد.

sentences.fa: لیلا جواب داد که اگر لازم باشد، مشکلی ندارد.
sentences.r: Leylā javāb dād ke agar lāzem bāshad, moshkel-i nadārad.
sentences.en: Leila answered that if it was necessary, she didn't mind.
sentences.faV: لَیلا جَواب داد که اَگَر لازِم باشَد، مُشکِلی نَدارَد.

sentences.fa: بعد از او خواستند که درباره‌ی بزرگ‌ترین اشتباهش صحبت کند.
sentences.r: ba'd az u khāstand ke darbāre-ye bozorg-tarin eshtebāh-ash sohbat konad.
sentences.en: Then they asked her to talk about her biggest mistake.
sentences.faV: بَعد اَز او خواستَند که دَرباره‌یِ بُزُرگ‌تَرین اِشتِباهَش صُحبَت کُنَد.

sentences.fa: لیلا با خنده تعریف کرد که یک بار یک ایمیل خصوصی را اشتباهی برای همه‌ی همکارانش فرستاده است.
sentences.r: Leylā bā khande ta'rif kard ke yek bār yek imeyl-e khosusi rā eshtebāhi barā-ye hame-ye hamkārān-ash ferestāde ast.
sentences.en: Laughing, Leila told them that she had once sent a private email to all her colleagues by mistake.
sentences.faV: لَیلا با خَنده تَعریف کَرد که یِک بار یِک ایمَیلِ خُصوصی را اِشتِباهی بَرایِ هَمه‌یِ هَمکارانَش فِرِستاده اَست.

sentences.fa: در پایان، مدیر قول داد که تا آخر هفته به او خبر بدهد.
sentences.r: dar pāyān, modir ghowl dād ke tā ākhar-e hafte be u khabar bedahad.
sentences.en: At the end, the manager promised to let her know by the end of the week.
sentences.faV: دَر پایان، مُدیر قَول داد که تا آخَرِ هَفته به او خَبَر بِدَهَد.

sentences.fa: امروز صبح منشی شرکت زنگ زد و گفت که لیلا را استخدام کرده‌اند.
sentences.r: emruz sobh monshi-ye sherkat zang zad o goft ke Leylā rā estekhdām karde-and.
sentences.en: This morning the company's secretary rang and said they had hired Leila.
sentences.faV: اِمروز صُبح مُنشیِ شِرکَت زَنگ زَد و گُفت که لَیلا را اِستِخدام کَرده‌اَند.

sentences.fa: منشی پرسید که آیا می‌تواند از شنبه‌ی آینده شروع کند.
sentences.r: monshi porsid ke āyā mi-tavānad az shanbe-ye āyande shoru' konad.
sentences.en: The secretary asked whether she could start next Saturday.
sentences.faV: مُنشی پُرسید که آیا می‌تَوانَد اَز شَنبه‌یِ آیَنده شُروع کُنَد.

options: to let her know by the end of the week

questions.q: Which words introduce a reported yes/no question?

sections.title: Passing on messages – and greetings
sections.md:
Persian has a small grammar of its own for passing things on. When someone cannot talk to you directly, they ask a friend to [[سلام برساند|salām beresānad|deliver their greeting]], and your friend reports it: [[مینا سلام رساند|Minā salām resānd|Mina sends her regards]]. As you leave a house you will hear [[به خانواده سلام برسانید|be khānevāde salām beresānid|give my regards to your family]], and you answer [[چشم، حتماً|cheshm, hatman|I will, of course]].

In the news, reported speech has its own fixed phrases. A report rarely begins with گفت; instead you read [[به گفته‌ی پلیس…|be gofte-ye polis…|according to the police…]], [[به نقل از خبرگزاری…|be naghl az khabargozāri…|quoting the news agency…]] or [[وی افزود که…|vey afzud ke…|he added that…]] – with [[وی|vey]], the formal written word for *he* or *she*, which you will almost never hear in conversation.

And when Iranians tell a story among friends, they love direct speech, often in the present tense for drama: [[بهش می‌گم: «چرا؟» می‌گه: «همین‌طوری!»|behesh mi-gam: «cherā?» mi-ge: «hamin-towri!»|so I say to him, 'Why?' And he says, 'No reason!']]

sections.title: Tips
items: Don't shift the tense: 'he said he was tired' is گفت خسته است. گفت خسته بود would mean that he had been tired before.
آیا belongs to writing and formal speech. In conversation, report a yes/no question with … یا نه: پرسید میای یا نه.
Never use آیا with a question word: پرسید کجا می‌روم, not *پرسید آیا کجا می‌روم.
Ask someone a question: از کسی پرسیدن. Ask someone to do something: از کسی خواستن که + subjunctive. Tell someone: به کسی گفتن.
The perfect (رفته است) is also the tense of rumour and inference: ظاهراً دیروز رفته است 'apparently he left yesterday'. If you hear it in a story, the speaker probably didn't see it happen.
In speech که is usually dropped (گفت فردا میاد); in writing it is usually kept (گفت که فردا می‌آید).

items.en: He said he would come tomorrow.
Sara said she was very tired.

items.fa: از من پرسید که ___ قهوه می‌خواهم.
items.r: az man porsid ke ___ ghahve mi-khāham.
items.en: He asked me whether I wanted coffee.
items.hint: the written marker of a yes/no question

items.fa: دکتر به من گفت که سیگار ___.
items.r: doktor be man goft ke sigār ___.
items.en: The doctor told me not to smoke.

items.fa: رضا گفت که کیفش را در تاکسی جا ___ است.
items.r: Rezā goft ke kif-ash rā dar tāksi jā ___ ast.
items.en: Reza said he had left his bag in the taxi.

items.fa: مدیر قول داد که تا فردا به ما خبر ___.
items.r: modir ghowl dād ke tā fardā be mā khabar ___.
items.en: The manager promised to let us know by tomorrow.

items.q: [[«من ایرانی هستم.»|«man irāni hastam.»]] How do you report it – 'He said he was Iranian'?
items.explain: Keep the tense, change the person. ایرانی بود would mean he used to be Iranian; ایرانی هستم is a direct quote.

items.q: Which sentence reports the question [[کجا کار می‌کنی؟|kojā kār mi-koni?]]?
options: پرسید که آیا کجا کار می‌کنم.
items.explain: Wh-questions keep their question word and never take آیا.

items.q: [[از ما خواست که ساکت باشیم.|az mā khāst ke sāket bāshim.]] means…
options: He wanted to be quiet with us.
He asked us to be quiet.
We asked him to be quiet.
items.explain: از کسی خواستن که + subjunctive = to ask someone to do something.
اعتراف کردن is 'to admit', اصرار کردن 'to insist'.

items.q: Which is the natural spoken way to report 'He asked if I was coming'?
items.explain: آیا belongs to writing; the spoken version ends with یا نه.

items.q: [[گفت که دیروز رفته است.|goft ke diruz rafte ast.]] Why the perfect رفته است?
options: It reports a past event the speaker only heard about.
It is a mistake for رفت.
items.explain: The perfect is the usual tense for reported, second-hand past events.

items.en: She said she was a doctor.
He asked me where the station was.
items.fa: از من پرسید که ایستگاه کجاست.
items.r: az man porsid ke istgāh kojāst.
items.faV: اَز مَن پُرسید که ایستگاه کُجاست.

items.en: I asked them whether they had seen the film.
items.fa: از آن‌ها پرسیدم که آیا فیلم را دیده‌اند.
items.r: az ān-hā porsidam ke āyā film rā dide-and.
items.faV: اَز آن‌ها پُرسیدَم که آیا فیلم را دیده‌اَند.

items.en: The teacher told us to open our books.
items.fa: معلم به ما گفت که کتاب‌هایمان را باز کنیم.
items.r: mo'allem be mā goft ke ketāb-hā-yemān rā bāz konim.
items.faV: مُعَلِّم به ما گُفت که کِتاب‌هایِمان را باز کُنیم.

items.en: He promised he would call me.
items.fa: قول داد که به من زنگ بزند.
items.r: ghowl dād ke be man zang bezanad.
items.faV: قَول داد که به مَن زَنگ بِزَنَد.

items.en: They said the shop would be closed tomorrow.
items.fa: گفتند که مغازه فردا بسته است.
items.r: goftand ke maghāze fardā baste ast.
items.faV: گُفتَند که مَغازه فَردا بَسته اَست.

items.fa: مینا گفت که امشب دیر می‌آید.
items.r: Minā goft ke emshab dir mi-āyad.
items.en: Mina said she would be late tonight.
items.faV: مینا گُفت که اِمشَب دیر می‌آیَد.

items.fa: از او پرسیدم که آیا گرسنه است.
items.r: az u porsidam ke āyā gorosne ast.
items.en: I asked him whether he was hungry.
items.faV: اَز او پُرسیدَم که آیا گُرُسنه اَست.

items.fa: مدیر از ما خواست که صبر کنیم.
items.r: modir az mā khāst ke sabr konim.
items.en: The manager asked us to wait.
items.faV: مُدیر اَز ما خواست که صَبر کُنیم.

items.fa: رضا قول داد که دیگر دیر نکند.
items.r: Rezā ghowl dād ke digar dir nakonad.
items.en: Reza promised not to be late again.
items.faV: رِضا قَول داد که دیگَر دیر نَکُنَد.

items.en: He said he couldn't come tomorrow.
options: He said he couldn't come tomorrow.
He asked if he could come tomorrow.

items.fa: پرسید که آیا شما ایرانی هستید.
items.r: porsid ke āyā shomā irāni hastid.
items.en: He asked whether you were Iranian.
options: He asked whether you were Iranian.
He asked where you were from.
items.faV: پُرسید که آیا شُما ایرانی هَستید.

items.fa: از من خواست که در را ببندم.
items.r: az man khāst ke dar rā bebandam.
items.en: She asked me to close the door.
options: She asked me to close the door.
She asked me to open the door.
She wanted to close the door.
items.faV: اَز مَن خواست که دَر را بِبَندَم.
